messages:
maya: heads-up — saw a regression on staging for FlashAttn-v2 variant when we hit mixed seq lengths. p99 latency spikes and a couple of NaNs from the model. Repro script attached below.

sam: can you paste the profiler output? is this a kernel hang or numeric instability?

maya: early evidence points to numeric overflow in the softmax path under fp16 accumulation for long sequences + high head dims. nvprof shows reducing SM occupancy right before the NaN burst. snippet:

```
# nvprof summary
Kernel: flash_attn_v2_forward  Runtime: 12.4ms  registers: 64  sm_eff: 72%  divergent_warps: 3.2%
----
logsumexp max: 1.5e+38  -> inf  (likely exponent overflow in exp())
```

jin: interesting — sounds like the classic exp overflow (qk dot product too large). did we already clamp pre-softmax or use log-sum-exp stable reduction?

maya: v2 kernel assumes pre-scaling by 1/sqrt(dk) but we found cases where intermediate `qk_max` across tiles exceeded float16 range due to accumulation and lack of upcast. FlashAttn-v1 had an explicit upcast accumulator (bf16/float32) for the reduction; v2 avoids it for perf.

leo: also saw batching weirdness — the hybrid batcher groups by request count not tokens, so some batches have a few long seqs with many short ones. Those few long ones push the tiled qk into ranges that overflow when kernels expect uniform lengths.

sam: can you share the reproducer commands?

maya: repro (staging):
```
# small repro
python tools/repro_flash2_nan.py --model r-instruct --batch-sizes "[1,4,8]" --seq-dist long-tail
# produces NaNs within ~200 iterations on p3.2x
```

jin: I ran a local trace. The KV cache bookkeeping in paged-attn path mis-indexed when tiling boundaries aligned with cached block edges — ended up double-counting some keys in the reduction buffer and increasing the effective qk magnitude. I can share a perf trace.

leo: that explains a lot. double-counting would blow up sums quickly. does this only hit tiled/paged code?

jin: so far yes — fused flash kernels that do in-kernel accumulation are sensitive. Non-fused fallback (separate matmul + softmax) avoided NaNs because we upcast during reduction.

maya: we tested a naive mitigation: clamp pre-softmax using a dynamic shift: subtract max(qk_tile) per tile, and force the reduction accumulator to bf16. that prevented NaNs in 10k iter run but cost ~6% median latency on the hot path.

sam: tradeoff acceptable short-term. can we be smarter: detect likely overflow via a cheap max-abs probe and switch kernel? kernel selector could route to upcasting variant for batches where probe > threshold.

jin: exactly the plan I sketched: add a small pre-kernel pass that scans q/k heads  (cheap vectorized max) and returns a `scale_hint`. Kernel selector rules: if scale_hint > T1 -> use safe-upcast kernel; if between T0..T1 -> use per-tile clamp + bf16; else -> fast path. This keeps perf for the common case.

leo: also tweak batching heuristic: prefer group-by-token-count and a soft cap on long-seq mixing. If we pad-to-multiple-of-8 and avoid mixing >40x length ratio in same batch, incidence drops drastically.

perf-bot: nightly-bench: https://bench-redwood/test/flash2/1979 shows p99 spike reduced from 420ms -> 180ms on canary with batching change + selector fallback.

maya: good. action items:
- jin: prototype `scale_hint` probe + selector (PR)
- sam: update hybrid batcher to token-grouping heuristic and pad-to-vec multiple
- leo: add unit test that simulates tiled KV-edge alignments and double-counting case
- maya: run 48h canary with gated selector and upcast fallback, measure latency and cost delta

jin: note on numeric strategy — prefer bf16 accumulation for reductions (cheap on Ampere+). fp32 only when bf16 insufficient. Also consider small pre-softmax `min_clip` to avoid exp under/overflow on pathological inputs.

sam: about rollout: feature flag `flash2_safe_mode` gating upcast fallback + probe + batcher changes. default off on prod for 24h, on Canary for all staging.

leo: I will add a perf regression dashboard to track token-normalized cost and p99 latency per model variant.

maya: thanks — PRs please tag #eng-runtime and link perf runs. ping me when the canary is live. :thumbsup:

jin: quick note: quantized fp8 experiments should be paused for this kernel until we stabilize numeric guardrails — mixing fp8 accumulation with these edge-case double-count sums is a bad combo.

maya: agree. pause fp8 tests on FlashAttn-v2 until we have deterministic guards.

perf-bot: nightly diff created: https://bench-redwood/diff/1979742000-tiling-batch-kv

sam: I'll start the batcher PR today.

maya: thanks team — keeping this thread for audit and follow-ups.
